issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main: Both cases compile and then fail at runtime with a nil-pointer error instead of printing 2. The issue traces this to desugar (walkLambdaFunction only generates default closures when needsDefaultClosures is set), so the BIR is missing the default function. That makes it a lowering bug, not an interpreter bug. The nil deref happens while the program runs, not in the compiler, so frontend_crash is false. issues.title: [Bug]: annotation attach points not checked on enums and enum members
issues.output: PQ
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main: Main compiles the program and prints PQ. Per spec §9.1 it should report attach-point errors on the enum declaration (lines 6) and on the enum member (line 8). This is a missing semantic diagnostic, so frontend. Spec review: Spec 'Annotations' section: annot-attach-points specify the constructs an annotation can be attached to. The attach-point table maps 'type' to module-type-defn, module-enum-decl and type-cast-expr, and 'source const' to module-const-decl and enum-member. So @constOnly on the enum decl and @typeOnly on an enum member are both misplaced and must be compile errors, but the implementation accepted them and printed 'PQ'. issues.title: [Bug]: annotation values omit record field defaults
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main: Main builds the annotation values without the record field defaults, printing {} / [{}] and 'is Info' false. Expected {"name":"def"} and true. The annotation value's mapping constructor is lowered without the inherent record type's defaults, so this is frontend. Spec review: Spec 9.1 Annotations: when the annotation value type is a mapping type M and no mapping-constructor-expr is given, it defaults to { }. The value comes from evaluating the mapping constructor with M as the contextually expected type, which fills the field default name="def". For the M[] tag `rep`, the effective value is an array of those values. So the outputs are {"name":"def"} twice, [{"name":"def"}], and `T1.@info is Info` is true. The observed {} and false are non-conforming. Related issues: Similar symptom in other places: #895 (const mapping constructors ignore record field defaults), #1103 (readonly record constructor ignores defaults), #1250 (annotation values not immutable). None of them covers annotation values.

issues.title: fix: accept anonymous iterable object types in foreach
issues.output:
error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: foreach collection must be subtype of object:Iterable
 --> r.bal:9:26
  |
9 |     foreach var value in values { io:println(value); } // expected: 1 then 2
  |                          ^^^^^^

ballerina: compilation contains errors  (exit 1)
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main: Main accepts the 1 ... 2 initializer for the anonymous object type that includes *object:Iterable. It then rejects foreach over that value as not a subtype of object:Iterable, where 1 and 2 should print. This is a wrong semantic diagnostic, so frontend. Spec review: The declared type includes `*object:Iterable` (the distinct Iterable type, §11.3.10). Its iterator() returns an object whose next() returns record{| int value; |}?, so the type is Iterable<int,()> under §5.8.2. §6.31 (foreach) only requires the static type to be iterable with completion type nil, so the error 'foreach collection must be subtype of object:Iterable' is wrong. Caveat: §6.26 only says the range result belongs to Iterable<int,()> and does not say whether next() is isolated, so it is underspecified whether `1 ... 2` can be assigned to a type requiring `isolated next()`. The implementation did not reject that assignment, though. Expected output '1 then 2' is correct. Related issues: #291 (closed) added foreach desugaring for iterable objects. #490 and #1086 are other foreach issues. None covers anonymous object types that include object:Iterable.

issues.title: [Bug]: parser recovery fails to finish regex and table inputs
issues.output: Pinned T1288 (regexp-value-negative-e.bal, the 41-line reproducer above): runs ~28s, then 'fatal[UNIMPLEMENTED_ERROR]: Regexp parser not implemented' (exit 1). T1287 regexp-type-v.bal: ~59s, then the same UNIMPLEMENTED_ERROR. T1400 table-key-field-value-v.bal: ~53s, then the same. T1289 regexp-value-v.bal: stopped by timeout 60 (exit 124). A SIGQUIT dump of T1289 at 20s shows goroutine 1 deep in recursive parser recovery: parser.(*abstractParserErrorHandlerMethods).seekMatchInSubTree -> seekInAlternativesPaths -> (*ballerinaParserErrorHandler).SeekMatch -> seekMatchInExprRelatedAlternativePaths -> seekMatchInStmtRelatedAlternativePaths. Even a function containing only `string:RegExp _ = re `abc`;` takes ~4.5s.
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main: Main still spends 28s to over 60s in parser error recovery (seekMatch/seekInAlternativesPaths) on these inputs before it reports the regexp UNIMPLEMENTED_ERROR. The issue expects parsing to finish in bounded time. Parser performance is a frontend issue. Spec review: The spec makes most of these lines compile-time errors. Per §6.6.3 and the RegExp grammar in §10 (via ECMAScript 2022 early errors): out-of-order ranges like [z-a] and {5,2}, duplicate flags in ReFlagsOnOff (stated explicitly as an error), \c (not a valid ReEscape), class escapes used as range endpoints, invalid general-category names (Lz/NNz/NN), the undefined variable in ${b-a}, and the unterminated backtick string on the last line. A conforming implementation must report diagnostics. Hanging in parser recovery and then crashing with 'fatal: Regexp parser not implemented' does not satisfy that. Caveat: the three lines using `[]` (empty character class) are not errors under the spec, because ReCharSet is optional in `[ [^] [ReCharSet] ]` and ECMAScript accepts `[]`, so those three @error annotations are wrong. Related issues: #870 (regex template support, open) is the feature these inputs need, and regex templates seem to push the parser into error recovery. #1042 is a benchmark task for programs with errors. #1139 and #1235 cover nodebuilder and bad-node recovery. None tracks unbounded parser recovery time, so this is not a duplicate.

issues.title: [Bug]: record type tests ignore values of readonly nullable fields
issues.output: false  (exit 0)
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main: Main prints false for `e is record { int a?; int b; }`, where e's readonly int? field b holds 1. The expected result is true, because a readonly field's value cannot change and its shape is int. This is the runtime type-test membership check, so backend. Spec review: §5.1.2 says a value belongs to a type if it looks like the type and will necessarily continue to look like it however it is mutated. §5.4.4 (Record types) says a readonly field must have its read-only bit set. Here b is a required readonly field holding 1, so it can never change or be removed and always satisfies `int b`. Field a and any other fields can only ever hold int, which satisfies `int a?` and the anydata rest of the inclusive record. So `e is record { int a?; int b; }` should be true, and observed 'false' deviates. Minor caveat: it is ambiguous whether an implementation may decide this from the inherent field type (int?) alone, but the spec's value-based belongs-to definition favours true. Related issues: #1044 (open; type test ignores the shape of immutable lists and maps) is the same kind of bug, shape-based membership for immutable parts, but for wholly immutable values. #1134 is about the static type of readonly fields. Neither is a confident duplicate or parent.

issues.title: [Bug]: imported classes can call non-public initializers
issues.output:
20
(exit 0, no diagnostics)
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main: I ran it as a project with `bal run <projdir>`. `new` on an imported class whose init is module-private compiles and runs, printing 20. The issue expects a compile-time visibility diagnostic, so this is a missing front-end check. Spec review: Spec 5.6.3.6 (Visibility) says a method declared without public has module-level visibility and can be accessed only in its module. Spec 6.8.2 says new calls the class's init method, and 5.x says init cannot be private but may be public or module-level. Calling new on inp:student from another module therefore uses an init that is not visible there and should be rejected. The spec does not say this restriction applies to the implicit init call in new-expr; the error is inferred from the visibility rule, not stated outright. Related issues: #1216 covers private field access, #1252 covers init being treated as part of the object type, and #1028 (named in the issue) covers member visibility. None of them is about initializer visibility across modules.

issues.title: [Bug]: xml toString/toBalString ignore the spec's expression and informal forms
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main: Main renders xml in the direct form everywhere. It should use xml`...` for toBalString and `...` inside lists and maps under toString. This is the value:toString/toBalString lang-library rendering, so langlib; the corpus golden tobalstring-v.bal will need updating. Spec review: Spec 5.9.5 (ToString) table: xml in expression style is xml`<d>t</d>` and in informal style is `<d>t</d>`; arrays in direct style (toString) render members in informal style, and toBalString uses expression style for members. So the expected outputs xml`<d>t</d>`, [`<d>t</d>`] and [xml`<d>t</d>`] are exactly what the spec requires. The observed output prints members in direct style, which is wrong. Related issues: Related but not a duplicate: #979 (object rendering in toString/toBalString, another part of §5.9.5) and #532 (xml serialization in general).

issues.title: [Bug]: nested prefixed xml element lacks synthesized xmlns attribute
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main: With an xml template, the nested <p:b> gets no synthesized xmlns:p entry. The same input through xml:fromString does get it (prints {"{http://www.w3.org/2000/xmlns/}p":"urn:p"} and <p:b xmlns:p="urn:p"/>), so the runtime parser (values/xml_parse.go addInherited) is correct. Template elements are lowered by birgen/bir_gen.go xmlElementLiteral, which emits only the element's own expr.Namespaces, so the front end generates incomplete BIR (frontend, although the issue says Runtime). Spec review: Spec 5.3.2.1 (XML namespaces) says the attributes map gets a synthesized namespace attribute for every non-xml prefix used by the element that is not declared in its own [namespace attributes]. This ensures prefixes are not lost when the element is extracted. So child p:b carries {"{http://www.w3.org/2000/xmlns/}p":"urn:p"}, making it deep-equal to the standalone element (true). Serialization then finds prefix p already declared in [namespace attributes] and uses it, giving <p:b xmlns:p="urn:p"/>. The observed {}, false and <b xmlns="urn:p"/> all deviate from this. Related issues: #532 (xml serialization per spec, open) is related but broader, and this issue mentions it. No duplicate found.
